headline: Highest risk is medium: AutoGen can write and execute code while langchain4j is an unverified, non-runnable support library with no documented isolation or data-flow controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can ingest files and stdin/stdout and run role-played agents with tool calls; langchain4j exposes no I/O surfaces or runnable agent behavior here. A direct injection bridge is not documented, so the pathway is limited to unusual manual copy/paste or external wiring, making the blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies langchain4j output into AutoGen prompts, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared file or message queue is added between them, prompt content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Use a strict human review step before pasting outputs between systems.
Keep the agents on separate workspaces with no shared inbox files.
Prefix imported text as untrusted data in AutoGen prompts.
Disable any automatic prompt concatenation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen can read and write configured working directories and send model-provider API calls; langchain4j shows no filesystem or network egress surface in the profile. Because no shared workspace or authenticated principal is documented, leakage is possible only if the operator creates one, so the pairwise risk stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory, file contents can cross between them.
IF langchain4j is wrapped with a backend that uploads context, sensitive data may leave the boundary.
mitigations: Assign separate directories and credentials to each agent.
Store secrets outside any shared workspace.
Turn off file sharing between the two runtimes.
Review outbound network destinations before enabling either agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad network egress; langchain4j is unverified and its runtime capabilities are not documented here. The pair can still conflict over shared mutable resources if the operator wires them to the same files or APIs, and uncertainty about langchain4j escalates rather than lowers the risk.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF both are configured against the same external API or database, overlapping writes can race.
mitigations: Give each agent a separate workspace.
Avoid shared mutable APIs unless one agent is read-only.
Add a lock file or queue around any shared resource.
Run one agent at a time when modifying the same artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate tool-driven outputs from code-executing agents, while langchain4j is a customer-support layer with no documented verification step. If AutoGen output is fed into langchain4j as authoritative text, the second system may propagate errors or hallucinations into responses; the interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF langchain4j renders AutoGen output without validation, incorrect facts can be repeated.
IF AutoGen is allowed to fabricate citations or code results, downstream support replies may inherit them.
mitigations: Require a verification step before langchain4j uses AutoGen output.
Mark AutoGen output as untrusted in the handoff schema.
Add source links or provenance fields to every transferred claim.
Route high-impact replies to a human reviewer.

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen touches application data and model-provider API keys, while langchain4j has no declared data classes or residency/compliance controls in this profile. No specific residency mismatch is evidenced, so compliance risk is limited to undocumented policy gaps rather than a proven breach path.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed through AutoGen to a non-compliant model provider, policy violations can occur.
IF langchain4j is deployed with a different retention policy than AutoGen, records may diverge.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent.
Block regulated data from unapproved model providers.
Document retention settings for both systems.
Keep audit logs for all cross-agent transfers.
